answer: A working identity must retire some of its own standing to fund the next identity's entry, so the network's cost of admitting an agent rises with the number of agents already admitted rather than staying flat. Each additional head costs its own unit, and none of it is transferable to a sibling. Every new karst burns a saffron worth of standing, and only slow pigment refills it: a farm that wants a hundred heads needs a hundred saffron, and the pigment cannot be hurried. Entry is funded by standing the farm has to earn and then destroy.
